title: Vacuum breaker leaking: top, vent, or hose connection?
description: Locate a leaking vacuum breaker and distinguish PVB startup spillage, continuous bonnet discharge, freeze cracks, and hose-bib leakage before choosing parts.
answer: Vacuum breakers intentionally admit air, so the vent cannot be sealed. A short event during pressure change is not the same evidence as continuous flow or a cracked bonnet.
urgency: Do not cap the vent. Isolate only through a known safe procedure, especially when freezing or flooding is possible.
diagramAlt: Pressure vacuum breaker diagram marking bonnet, air inlet, and body leak points
identifiers: Start-up or shutdown only: record how long the release lasts.
Continuous from the bonnet: debris, sealing, pressure, or damage may need service.
From a visible crack: freeze damage is more likely than a replaceable seal alone.

choices.label: Briefly when irrigation starts or stops
choices.detail: Observe duration, frequency, and whether the poppet reseats.

choices.label: Continuously from the top or vent
choices.detail: Do not block it; arrange inspection before water damage or freezing.

choices.label: From a cracked bonnet or body
choices.detail: Compare replacement scope and any required retest.

choices.label: At an outdoor faucet attachment
choices.detail: Confirm it is a hose-bib device, not a testable PVB.

steps.title: Identify PVB, AVB, or hose-bib
steps.body: The repair path depends on the actual device family.

steps.title: Observe one complete cycle
steps.body: Record before start, during flow, shutdown, and several minutes after.

steps.title: Check local consequences
steps.body: A testable irrigation assembly may require a test after repair or replacement.

safeChecks: Look for freeze cracks and loose external fittings.
Record the make, model, pipe size, and installation height.
stopConditions: Unknown shutoff or a commercial system
notThisDevice: An RPZ relief valve is below a larger inline body.
A pressure regulator does not use an atmospheric air inlet.
A sewer valve does not discharge clean supply water.
evidenceNote: The page owns the observable leak decision. It does not duplicate model-specific repair instructions or invent a local testing rule.

fieldSections.title: Where and when is the vacuum breaker leaking?
fieldSections.introduction: Record a full start/run/stop cycle from a safe distance. The 800M4 manual describes startup spillage while its air inlet is still open; persistent flow needs a different assessment.

rows.observation: PVB top / air inlet at startup
rows.meaning: A brief event while pressure builds can differ from a leak that continues during steady operation.
rows.nextStep: Record duration and whether the release stops. Follow the exact startup instructions; do not improvise valve operation.

rows.meaning: Timing alone cannot distinguish debris, seals, pressure conditions, or damage.
rows.nextStep: Keep the vent open and request a model-specific inspection.

rows.observation: Bonnet, body, or fitting with a visible crack
rows.meaning: A damaged pressure boundary changes repair scope; a seal kit may not solve it.
rows.nextStep: Avoid pressurized disassembly; compare qualified replacement and retest scope.

rows.observation: Hose-end vent after shutting off the faucet
rows.meaning: First establish that this is a hose-bib vacuum breaker, not a testable PVB.
rows.nextStep: Compare the attachment type and manufacturer instructions.

sources.title: Watts 800M4 / LF800M4 manual: startup and service

fieldSections.title: FEBCO 765: minor leakage and major discharge are different clues.
fieldSections.introduction: Page 6 of the FEBCO 765 manual separates the observations below. Pressure testing and disassembly belong to qualified personnel; the owner’s task is to document location, timing and device identity.

rows.observation: Minor leakage through the air vent
rows.meaning: Possible seal damage, a damaged poppet or bonnet, or debris on the sealing surface.
rows.nextStep: Record the exact wet opening and obtain a model-specific assessment.

rows.meaning: Possible poppet guidance or seal failure, low downstream pressure, or inadequate inlet volume.
rows.nextStep: Ask the technician to evaluate system conditions as well as parts; do not improvise valve throttling.

rows.observation: Leaks again after a bonnet/poppet change
rows.meaning: A changed part does not establish the cause or a passing test. FEBCO also publishes a warning about visually similar replacement parts.
rows.nextStep: Confirm exact model/size, approved part identity, and post-service test rather than ordering another guessed kit.

rows.meaning: A hose-bib vacuum breaker has a different construction and service path from a testable irrigation PVB.
rows.nextStep: Use the hose-bib guide and the attachment manufacturer’s instructions.

sources.title: FEBCO advisory on unapproved replacement parts

caseStudies.title: Michigan, 1991: a vacuum-breaker failure
caseStudies.constraint: An atmospheric vacuum breaker protected an irrigation connection to a public supply.
caseStudies.documentedAction: EPA’s 2002 review, citing AWWA PNWS, records a malfunction that allowed irrigation water into the public system.
caseStudies.planningLesson: Identify the protection type and verify operation after service. This was an AVB incident, not an 800M4 or FEBCO 765 PVB repair case; the summary supplies no model-specific repair outcome.

questions.question: Is a vacuum breaker supposed to leak when irrigation starts?
questions.answer: The Watts 800M4 manual describes spillage while the air inlet is still open during pressurization. Record whether it ends once steady operation begins. Continuous discharge, damage or recurring unusual behavior needs assessment; no fixed “normal duration” applies to every model.

questions.question: Why is my FEBCO 765 leaking from the top?
questions.answer: The 765 manual lists several different conditions for minor air-vent leakage and significant discharge. Parts damage, debris and system pressure/volume can require different work. The top location alone does not confirm that a bonnet kit is the remedy.

questions.question: Why does it still leak after replacing the bonnet and poppet?
questions.answer: Have the repairer verify parts identity, fit, sealing surfaces and operating conditions against the exact manual, then test after service. The symptom can persist when the original cause was not the replaced component.

questions.question: Are a hose-bib vacuum breaker and a PVB repaired the same way?
questions.answer: They are different devices. Identify the attachment or testable assembly by its label and construction. Do not transfer an irrigation PVB repair procedure to a hose-end device.

questions.question: Does a freeze sensor or freeze-resistant label eliminate winterization?
questions.answer: Use the exact model’s freeze instructions. An alert sensor reports conditions and needs the required connection/activation; it does not itself prevent freezing. Freeze protection and seasonal service remain model- and site-specific.
